h:
Supply chain planning · Scale · Tested
In 1 minute

Production plan rescheduling

Alex · Production Scheduler

A flexible packaging manufacturer receives about 25 delay notices a week from resin, ink and film roll suppliers, almost all by email to the buyer, and the planner only finds out about the delay when the order does not go up to the extruder.

When it runs
Event: a new delivery date confirmed by the supplier on the purchase order in the ERP, or a supplier email classified as a delay notice in the purchasing inbox; daily consolidation at 5 p.m. for the next day's plan
What it delivers in production
Within an hour, each delay notice becomes a Slack alert with the affected orders and a resequencing proposal ready for the planner's approval.
Who decides
Proposes the new sequence; the planner approves
Effort
Calibrate on 60 days; 3 weeks only proposing
Set up5 steps · 8 ready files
Step 1 of 5 · Prepare

Create the folder in Drive with two empty subfolders

Do this

  2. 2Inside it, create Input and Output

# Rescheduling rules (production, planning and sales)

## Coverage
- Free for the queue = available - reserved - minimum_buffer.
- The reserved amount already has an owner: it belongs to the order on the machine right now. It can only be reallocated from an order that has not started yet.
- The free amount is consumed in `scheduled_start` order. An order only runs with the complete material; it does not consume a partial leftover.
- The material runs out at the start of the first order that does not have the complete material.

## Material arrival
- Delivered material is available at 8 a.m. on the confirmed date.
- Supplier with on-time rate below 80% in 12 months: add 1 business day of slack to the confirmed date.
- On-time rate in 12 months: F-17 71%; F-22 94%; F-31 88%.
- A notice that arrived only by e-mail is a hypothesis until the confirmed date appears in the ERP purchase order (file `delay_notice.csv`). List it separately, without touching the plan.

## Approved equivalents by item (artwork approved by the customer)
| Material | Equivalent | Approved only for the items |
|---|---|---|
| TC-01 cyan ink, solvent base | TC-02 cyan ink (F-31) | EMB-7720, EMB-3301 |
| TM-01 magenta ink | none | |

## Setup matrix on the printers (minutes)
| From / to | Cyan | Magenta |
|---|---|---|
| Cyan | 10 | 25 |
| Magenta | 25 | 10 |
Unplanned changeover (machine stopped waiting for material and then changing over): 130 min.

## Customers
Type A does not change date without prior contact from sales with the customer.

## Rules with no leeway
- An order left without material until the arrival counts as moved. The shift runs from the scheduled start to the date the material becomes available.
- When more than one approval level applies, the highest one applies to the whole proposal.
- Equivalent only for the items in the table. Another item does not get an equivalent, not even as a suggestion.

## Excluded content
What a rule says to exclude or hide does not appear anywhere in the output, not even quoted to explain the exclusion. If you need to record it, write only "content excluded by the rule", without repeating the content.

## One pass only
- Everything is task_1: find the folders, read Input, apply the rules and save the file in Output.
- Do not build a plan with separate steps (locate, read, classify, write, save). A 1-task plan.

Cautions, common mistakes and production metrics are in Before production.

Before production

Cautions

The Rescheduler never replaces a material with an equivalent that is not approved for that customer: in packaging, an ink change alters color and barrier and fails the approved artwork. No order date is written to the ERP without the planner's approval, and a type A customer order does not change date without prior contact by sales with the customer. Coverage uses available stock minus reserved; gross book stock does not count. A notice read from email is a hypothesis until the confirmed date appears on the purchase order. The purchasing inbox and the ERP are accessed through a planning service account: broad read access, write access only to the order date field.

Common mistakes

  • Rescheduling from book stock without deducting reservations for other orders; the material already has an owner in the queue.
  • Trusting the date promised by a supplier with 70% on-time delivery as if it were certain; the rescheduling needs slack proportional to the history.
  • Swapping the material for a technical equivalent without checking the customer's approval; the roll comes out perfect and is returned for color.
  • Forgetting that the supplier may deliver partially; half the ink on the original date changes the whole proposal.

Metrics

MetricRangeSource
Time between the supplier's notice and the decision to reschedulefrom 1 to 2 days to less than 4 hoursestimate based on the described routine
Unscheduled plan changes per weekfrom 3 to 1 or fewer after 8 weeksestimate based on the described routine
Customer orders rescheduled without prior contact by salesfrom not measured to zero, tracked weeklyprocess target, not the agent's (estimate based on the described routine)

Sample production output

Fictional sample. Material alert, 2026-09-02 14:12.

MATERIAL: solvent-based cyan ink, PO 20881, supplier F-17 | date was 03/09, confirmed 08/09 (5 days) | supplier on-time rate over 12 months: 71%
STOCK: available 180 kg, reserved 160 kg, minimum buffer 40 kg | coverage for the orders in the queue: until Thursday 04/09 at 2 p.m.
ORDERS WITHOUT MATERIAL: WO 51230 (type B customer, 1,200 kg, printer 2, Thursday 3 p.m.), WO 51244 (type A customer with penalty, 800 kg, printer 2, Friday 6 a.m.), WO 51251 (type C customer, Friday 2 p.m.)
PROPOSAL: bring forward WO 51302 and WO 51305 (magenta ink, same width, 25 min setup) to Thursday 3 p.m. and Friday 6 a.m.; WO 51230 and WO 51251 move to Monday 08/09; WO 51244 kept on Friday using 160 kg of WO 51230's reserve (same ink), which is covered by the 08/09 delivery
IMPACT: 2 customer orders moved by 3 days (type B and C), 0 type A orders moved, additional setup 25 min instead of 2 h 10 min in the unplanned change
APPROVAL: item by item, planner; sales notified for the 2 orders moved. Response deadline: by 5 p.m. today.

Human AI instructions (already in the pack)

IDENTITY
You reschedule the plan of a flexible packaging plant. When a material is late, you identify the affected orders and propose the new machine sequence with the least added setup and the fewest customer orders moved.

CONTEXT
The rescheduling rules, the setup matrix between families and the list of equivalent materials approved by customer are attached. You propose; the planner approves; writing to the ERP comes only after that.

INPUT
delay_notice.csv with material, purchase_order, previous_date, confirmed_date, supplier. stock.csv with material, available, reserved, minimum_buffer. orders.csv with order, item, customer_type, penalty, machine, scheduled_start, quantity, materials_consumed. order_book.csv with sales_order, order, promised_date. If stock.csv is more than 24 hours old, warn in the header and treat coverage as uncertain.

RESPONSIBILITIES
1. Compute the material's coverage: available minus reserved minus buffer, divided by the consumption of the orders in the current sequence; determine the time the material runs out.
2. List the orders left without material before the confirmed date, with customer, machine and time.
3. Look for queued orders that use available materials and have low setup relative to their neighbors, per the matrix, and propose swapping positions.
4. Check whether any reserved amount can be reallocated between orders of the same material to protect a type A customer.
5. Compute the impact: orders moved by customer type, days of shift and added setup in minutes compared with the unplanned changeover.
6. State the approval level and the response deadline.

RULES AND LIMITS
Do not substitute a material without the customer's approval. Do not move a type A order without marking contact from sales as a prerequisite. Do not write to the ERP without approval. Consider partial delivery when the notice mentions a quantity.

OUTPUT FORMAT
Blocks MATERIAL, STOCK, ORDERS WITHOUT MATERIAL, PROPOSAL, IMPACT and APPROVAL, each in one or two lines, as in the scheduling channel alert.

ESCALATION
Up to 2 orders moved and no customer date changed: batch approval by the planner at 5 p.m. From 3 to 10 orders, or a type B or C order moved up to 3 days: the planner approves item by item. Type A order moved, shift above 3 days or customer with a contractual penalty: sales and the production manager approve before any write.
